segmenti.tekst: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

Yusuf: after the king summoned these women who had enticed Yusuf to zina (fornication), and they confessed that Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam (peace be upon him), was innocent, that he was chaste, after that came also the confession of the prime minister's wife that it was she who had enticed him to evil, to zina, and that he was innocent.

When the king saw all of this – the king who, of course, had liked the interpretation of Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, the interpretation of his dream – he said to this envoy: "Bring him to me," but not just like that first "bring him to me", rather: "I will make him one of my close men", that is, one of his closest associates, "I will make him one of my closest associates."

And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says further: "فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ" – he says: "You are, from today, here with us, a highly esteemed man, and you are trustworthy."

That is, you will be a shield for everything that happens in the state. See how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, raised Yusuf up. After his brothers threw him away, and he was sold as a slave, and then the oppression of this woman – the oppression done to him by this woman and her husband – and then prison, in the end Allah, in the end Allah raises him up.
Did Yusuf, dear brothers, simply accept being a close associate of the king, enjoying himself in the palace, or did he want to do something more for that people and for the surrounding states?
You will see later. Believe me, among us, when people get some position or find themselves a cushy post somewhere, they only look at how to fill their own pockets.
That is the situation today, unfortunately. But Yusuf, alayhis-salam, did not want that. And that is why this story of his is special. What does Yusuf, alayhis-salam, say?

He says: "Make me," or "appoint me" minister of finance, the one who will take care of the finances. "Inni hafizun 'alim" – truly I know how to safeguard money, but also how to distribute it, in what way to spend it.

Now a logical question arises: we have a hadith narrated by Abdur-Rahman ibn Samurah from the Prophet, in which the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), says: "Ya Abdar-Rahman ibn Samurah, la tas'alil-imarah" – he says: "O Abdur-Rahman, do not," he says, "seek authority, do not seek authority.
Fa innaka in u'titaha 'an mas'alatin wukilta ilayha" – he says: "If you seek authority and then obtain it, you will be left, you will be left to yourself.

وَإِنْ أُعْطِيتَهَا عَنْ غَيْرِ مَسْأَلَةٍ أُعِنْتَ عَلَيْهَا" – "But if," he says, "you obtain authority without seeking it," he says, "you will be helped." Does this case of Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, now conflict with what the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, conveyed to us through Abdur-Rahman?

The scholars say: this is an exception, Yusuf is an exception, but not only Yusuf, rather anyone else who is a specialist in a certain matter like Yusuf, when at the given moment there is no one else to offer what he has to offer.

Had Yusuf not accepted to be at the head of the state, the state would have collapsed. So too the believer, when he sees or recognises an opportunity to improve the situation in a certain institution, in the city, should put himself forward. He should put himself forward in order to make his contribution.
But, as we said, not to fill his own pockets, but to work for the welfare of the people, for the welfare of society, so that society succeeds, as Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, did.
Did Yusuf stay only at words, or did he really do what he had asked for? It is said that Yusuf, the first thing when he came to power, sowed every inch of the land that was even a little fertile.
And the land that was not fertile, he fertilised and then sowed. The second thing, it is said, he built huge silos, huge storehouses, where he stored that food, that wheat.

And, it is said, the third thing: he spread awareness among ordinary people to save food. Because, believe me, dear brothers, in a time of plenty, when people are enjoying the blessings, it is hard to tell people: "Don't, people, spend a little less, save, save your wealth." Meaning, it is very hard.

Believe me, I studied there in Saudi Arabia, and the people there are, meaning, extremely rich. And now, to those people… As has been said: hard times give birth, give birth to strong men, and those nice, comfortable times give birth to weak ones.

So these generations of ours that grew up in those hard times are strong generations, they have lived through everything, while these generations now coming – may Allah just help us, nothing else. That is why, dear brothers, Yusuf did what he did, that is, he wanted to do something for that people, so that the people itself would benefit, and you will see later that those people too, that is, those states around Egypt, benefited.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَكَذَلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ" – and He says: thus We gave Yusuf authority in the land. This is, first of all, a message to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. I have said that this surah was revealed to Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in the hardest possible time, meaning when the Muslims literally had no way out. Meaning, that is the situation [unclear]. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, conveys to the Prophet: just as We granted Yusuf to be rescued from the well, to be saved

from slavery, to be delivered from prison, and after all that to become a ruler, We will grant it to you too, O Muhammad. And so Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, gave Yusuf authority. It says: he moved about Egypt as he wished, and as he wished.
"Nusibu bi rahmatina" – We bestow rahmah, mercy, on whomever We will. And this is not exclusively for Yusuf, but for everyone who works, who is good, who is honest.
Allah will not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost. Not only Yusuf's, but that of all who do good. Allah will not allow it: whoever does good will be repaid with good.
Whoever does good, Allah will repay him with good. That is what it says further. Meaning that Allah will not let the reward of those who do good be lost in this dunya (this world).

In this dunya, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says, He will give him a pleasant life, for as long as he lives, while he is here living. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say right after this verse? He says: but, He says, the reward of the Hereafter, the reward of the Hereafter is, He says, better for the believer and for the one who fears Allah.

It is all nice, the dunya is nice too, it is all nice, for a person to live peacefully, comfortably, but Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: but the reward in the Hereafter is better. "Lilladhina ahsanul-husna wa ziyadah" – He says: for those who do good deeds there is Jannah (Paradise), "wa ziyadah" – and, He says, looking at the Face of Allah. And the greatest blessing in Jannah is that they will look at the Face of Allah.

The greatest blessing. And what does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say, addressing the Prophet, He says: "وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الْأُولَى" – and, He says, the Hereafter is better for you than this world. And this world is nothing, dear brothers.
It passes. It passes very quickly. And so Yusuf obtained authority, authority in the land. In sha Allah, tomorrow we begin a new chapter, a new chapter in the life of Yusuf.

Also, it is very important, dear brothers, that we know: these days a series about Yusuf is being broadcast, I don't know on which channels. The first thing, meaning, that series which was filmed depicts the image of a prophet. Meaning, that is haram.

It is not permissible to depict the image of a prophet. By no means. Nor of the companions, they say, most scholars say. Nor of the companions, the image of the companions, let alone of a prophet. Second, that series is full of falsehoods and distorted things. You will see that, supposedly, Yusuf in the end marries that woman who enticed him to evil,

and she becomes young again, and so on. All of these are falsehoods, meaning unconfirmed things that have no foundation whatsoever. So a person should leave it, not watch it at all. Because whenever, you see, he now remembers Yusuf, the image of that actor comes to him, and Yusuf did not look like that at all. Allah knows what Yusuf looked like.

Or the image of Abu Bakr or Umar, and so on. So a person should avoid these things. That is why, dear brothers, we have the Book, and Allah has granted all of us the ability to read, or the lectures that our scholars have given on these topics. So a person should make an effort, make a little effort, to read and also to listen to a lecture or two. Now we will, in sha Allah, continue, continue further. May Allah grant you every good. As-salamu alaykum.
